Marta — thanks, and great to meet the team last week. I've pulled the key folks into thread and outlined responses below. High level: we can meet all asks, but we'll separate what is included in our standard Private offering vs. what is delivered via addendum or PS.

1) Operator access to customer keys (BYOK/HSM):
- Standard: Redwood's operator accounts never receive customer CMKs or plaintext key material when BYOK with an HSM is configured. The control plane will route key operations to customer-managed HSM endpoints or a customer-managed KMS; Redwood retains only references and encrypted metadata.
- Optional (addendum/PS): If GoodHealth requires an independent escrow arrangement (trusted third-party escrow of CMK metadata and recovery steps), we can offer a documented escrow path; final transfer mechanics are handled as a one-time professional services engagement.

2) Subprocessors:
- Standard: We will provide the current subprocessors list (region-filtered) and a short description of their role (e.g., telemetry ingestion, patch management supplier for our dedicated hosts).
- We include subprocessors that touch deployment control plane; for customer-controlled VPC with private control plane we'll exclude hosted telemetry collectors unless explicitly enabled.

3) Telemetry and operator logs:
- Standard: Operator actions (e.g., operator-run job ids, limited action types) are logged in audit trails and made available to customers; logs do not contain plaintext customer data or keys.
- We can provide a technical appendix showing log schemas and retention windows.

4) Attestations / 3rd party audits:
- Standard: We can share our most recent SOC-2 summary and an operator-attestation template describing operator privileges.
- Optional: Support for a customer-led third-party audit on a private deployment can be scheduled (PS + a scoped auditor access window).

Next steps proposed (mutual action plan):
- Redwood: provide subprocessors list + operator attestation template + sample log schema by EOD Wednesday (Aug 4). (Owner: Irene Choi)
- GoodHealth: confirm if escrow is required as a contractual deliverable or a PS option by Friday (Aug 6). (Owner: Marta)
- Schedule a 30-minute infra deep-dive with Alan and Karthik to validate KMS/HSM handshake (Target: week of Aug 9). (Owner: Aditya to coordinate)

I'll attach the operator-attestation-template and SOW excerpt in my next mail.

Best,

Alan / Marta — quick technical clarifications from Redwood's runbook perspective so your infra team can validate:

- BYOK/HSM model we recommend: customer HSM in their VPC with an RPC gateway. Redwood issues no key material. All cryptographic ops are performed by the customer's HSM; our runtime only receives ciphertext pointers.
- Operator model: Redwood operators may perform platform maintenance tasks (node health checks, kernel updates) but do not run key ops. Operator-facing tooling surfaces actions as ticketed jobs; the job payload lacks key plaintext and contains only a reference id and the minimal request metadata (timestamp, job id, operator id).
- Telemetry toggles: for private control plane we provide a 'minimal telemetry' profile that emits only anonymized operational metrics and redacted audit events; default retention 90 days, extendable by contract.
- Escrow path options we support: (a) customer-managed escrow with handshake doc (no transfer without customer approval) — no standard change to infra; (b) third-party escrow (trusted notary) — requires contract and PS to finalize; (c) Redwood-managed emergency key recovery only with explicit contractual SLAs and limited escrow custody model.

Technical attachments I've uploaded to the shared Drive: a log schema, sample audit event, and the subprocessors CSV filtered for US-only deployments. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-GoodHealth-DPA

Please let me know if Alan wants a short walkthrough of the handshake flow — happy to do a 30-minute screen share and step through a mock rotation and an emergency recovery scenario.

- Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

- Good: operator logs do not contain plaintext or key material. The reference-only job payload model matches our security bar.
- Escrow: GoodHealth prefers option (a) — customer-managed escrow with a signed handshake. We will not require Redwood-managed custody. We will, however, need a documented playbook describing the emergency recovery invocation steps (who signs off, what logs are required).
- Subprocessors: the US-only subprocessors CSV looks reasonable; procurement will use this to populate our vendor matrix.

Procurement note: if Redwood can include a short DPA exhibit listing the minimal telemetry toggles and retention windows and confirm PS rates for escrow setup, we can proceed to finalize the PO.
